doc: v2 — predictions tightened per A014 (closeout). Each prediction has rationale + tightening rationale.

predictions.rationale: PROJECT_STATUS_REPORT used 110 ms/iter (5s/step ÷ 45 iter/step). Tightened from [50, 200] because the calculation is layered estimate, but the underlying log shows 5±0.5s/step in the early-phase data. Realistic range ±35%.

predictions.metric: wall_seconds_median (AMGx fresh single-shot, 500K LPBF pd, lab GPU RTX 5060)
predictions.rationale: Existing npz meta shows 9-39s on dev RTX 3050. Lab 5060 (sm_120, 8GB, newer) likely 1.5-3× faster ⇒ 5-25s. Tightened upper bound from 50 to 25 because if it's >25s on lab GPU, the wrapper has serious overhead and we should investigate.

Hypothesis: update_coefficients ~30-100ms + solve at ~5-15s but reuse-of-hierarchy may speed convergence. Realistic range 0.2s (if amortization works well) to 3s (if mostly solve). Tightened from [50, 5000].

If setup ≈ 2-3s out of single solve 10-25s, amortizing setup over 6 steps saves only (5×3s)/(6×15s) ≈ 17% ⇒ 1.2× speedup. Conservatively 1.05-2.5. Refutes 100-1000× claim from S1 — within this experiment alone.
Tightened: in LPBF physics dominated by alpha jumps in <5% of cells, x_t-x_{t-1} similarity is high ⇒ warm-start should save 10-60% iter. Outside 10-60% would be surprising.
x evolves smoothly except at melt-front cells. Tightened upper to 30% (from 50%) — if >30% then warm-start is useless and the physics is even more chaotic than I think.
Conversation history showed 69-75s. Tightened from [40, 150] to ±30% because we have 6 lab-Xeon CHOLMOD runs already (conversation paste) and they were tightly clustered.

Tightened: symbolic part is ~30-50% of factor cost; reusing it should save that ⇒ 1.4-2× speedup. Lower bound 1.2× allows for some setup reuse but inplace overhead. If <1.2× then reuse is failing (numerical fallback). Upper 3× is generous for the case where matrix structure happens to be very symbolic-friendly.
Conversation history showed 1.13e-11. Tightened: anything <1e-12 or >1e-10 would mean either AMGx + IR is over-converging (impossible — bounded by fp64 floor) or the code has a bug.
Tightened: OF tol=1e-8 × κ_eff (~10^3-10^4 in well-conditioned subspace) → 1e-5 to 1e-4. Conversation showed 3.47e-5. If <5e-6 or >2e-4 then κ_eff is way off our model.
Tonight's audit measured 3.2e14 with seed-stable Lanczos. Tightened to ±1 order of magnitude. If outside, Lanczos seed sensitivity returns or we have a numerical regression.
Tightened upper from 1e16 to 1e14: single_track has rays>0 so b is non-trivial; expect κ smaller than lab32's 3.2e14. Wide range because we genuinely don't know — this is a NEW measurement.
Tonight's H11 svds gave [1.15e-16, 1.44e-15, ..., 9.29e-15]. Re-running on Xeon should give similar. Cluster (gap σ_2/σ_1 < 100) confirms near-null subspace structure.

If single_track matrix is well-conditioned (rays>0 → physical b), σ_min should be 1e-10 to 1e-6, isolated. If it ALSO has near-null cluster, then near-null structure is universal to LPBF pd matrices regardless of physics — important for paper narrative.

comparison_method.FAIL: value outside 2× of range bounds — interesting case (refutes hypothesis or reveals bug)

tightening_rationale: v1 ranges spanned 2-3 orders of magnitude in places, providing weak refutation power. v2 tightens to ranges that would actually reject hypotheses if measurement disagrees. New entries E09 svds (k=10) added per P8.
